    A wayfinding review of The Document · Patina designer portal

    The
    Wayfinding
    Review

    Nine seats walked one week of a designer's work through the paper. Two directions come back with the same data in two shapes.

    2026 · 08 · 25 Prepared for the Patina studio team Verified against main@695addb5f

    The standing complaint about The Document is four words long: “designers have to hunt for things.” The pilot designer left for the legacy portal twice. This review took that literally — it is scoped to one question, asked across the whole surface: is it always obvious what to do next, and how to reach the thing you need? Nothing here has been built. What follows is what the paper actually does today, four practitioners saying so in their own words, and two directions drawn on one specimen.

    The three rulings this work was given

    Doctrine
    Direction A tightens within doctrine. Direction B may amend it — every amendment named by its ledger id, its clause quoted, its trade and its rollback stated.
    Evidence
    Local dev, both flag states, no production walk. Everything cited below was rendered and read on a machine, not remembered.
    Baseline
    Both compositions — today's paper with worktable off, and the Worktable with it on. Each direction says how it lands on each.

    Contents

      The ask, and the method

      What was asked, and how we read the paper

      Review the designer portal's document interface — layout, navigation, flow — with a UX / UI team and an interior-design practitioner team both at the table, and come back with two directions that make it always obvious what to do next and how to reach the items a designer needs.

      The surface under review is The Document: /desk and /doc/[id] — one paper per engagement, a fixed seven-section spine from brief through care — plus the Studio Drawer, ⌘K, the g chords, the rooms block, the five shelves and the Drafting Room, across three width tiers: a bottom bar under 1180, a compact icon rail from 1180 to 1439, and the full spine with margin rail and shelved blocks at 1440 and above. It carries an append-only decision ledger through I143 and eight design decks in forty-five days. Two of the most severe findings ever recorded against it have never been ruled on: T4, no fleet view — “show me everything in install” has no path — and T2, install is a label on project mode, not a mode. And the worktable stage-adaptive composition, ruled “the destination” on 2026·08·15, is merged behind a fail-closed flag and had never been rendered for a human before this week.

      The method, in one paragraph

      We booted the portal against a local database, lifted five documents up the state ladder by RPC so every stage had a real paper to photograph, and took 86 verified screenshots at 1440, 1280 and 390 across both flag states — including the first render of the Worktable's four tables anyone has looked at. Then nine seats walked the same sixteen-task script over that evidence in one sitting, as one week of work: five UX / UI lenses (information architecture, interaction and next-action clarity, hierarchy across the width tiers, content and lexicon, reach — keyboard, mobile, accessibility) and four practitioners (a solo principal with six live jobs, the principal of a three-person studio, a junior in her first week, and an FF&E-and-procurement-heavy designer). A Chrome probe drove the live surface for the things a screenshot cannot answer — the Esc chain, the seven chords, scroll-spy, fold persistence, focus return. The nine seats returned 203 raw findings, which merged to 101, which then met three refuters in separate contexts — one checking the code, one checking the decision ledger, one re-driving the browser. A finding survived only if none of the three killed it. 92 survived; 9 were killed. Only the 92 are quoted below.

      Why the nine that died matter

      Eight were killed by the code — a seat reported an absence that turned out to be present, just not where they looked. The Orders ledger does print each PO's send and acknowledgement lifecycle in its provenance line. The FF&E line unfold on the paper is PO detail, movement and receiving, with a claim lifecycle and an inspection drawer mounted in place. A date move does draw a full ripple preview — a dashed ghost layer with moved boundaries and dated labels. Close the book and Begin the Direction are both genuinely disabled while their blockers stand. One more was killed by re-driving the browser. This is the shape of the whole problem: the capability is usually built, and unfound. Nothing in this deck cites a killed finding as a fact.

      Where this evidence stops

      • Local seeds, not production. Every screenshot came from a local Supabase with the repo's own seed data and three transient rich seeds re-applied by hand. No production walk was taken, and none is claimed.
      • Synthetic data. The specimen documents are fixtures. Where the seed had no project carrying both rooms and an active project section, the room-lens probe could not run at all — that gap is reported as a gap, not filled in from source.
      • No human designer in the loop. The four practitioner seats are grounded in Patina's own Leah sessions and prior audits, but they are readings of the evidence, not a re-walk with a working designer. Every obviousness score below is a seat's rating of a screenshot, and should be read ordinally.
      • A dev server, not a build. Load timings were recorded and are not cited as performance evidence. Redis was not running (127.0.0.1:6379 refused), so any Redis-backed path in the orders and projects services was unexercised; nothing on this surface depends on one.
      • The shots carry the dev server's own furniture. A small dark circular mark at the bottom-left of some screenshots is the Next.js dev-tools indicator, not a product control — a seat filed it as an unexplained badge overlapping page content, and the code refuter killed the finding for exactly that reason. Read past it.
      • Out of scope by instruction: the internals of Library, People and Room View, the client portal, iOS, and any schema change. Nothing was built into the product; the decision ledger was not appended to.

      The reading

      Sixteen tasks, one week, nine seats

      Every seat ran the same sixteen tasks in the same order, in one sitting, as one designer's week — and was told never to skip a task because it obviously has no path. Narrate the search instead; the search is the finding.

      Each task was rated twice, on a scale where 1 is could not find it, 3 is second-guessed myself and 5 is without thinking: once for knowing what to do, once for knowing how to get there. The numbers below are the mean of the nine seats' own tables. They are readings of rendered evidence by nine agents, not a timed re-walk with a working designer — read them as a ranking, not a measurement.

      The findings that matter most

      Below: every surviving blocker, and every finding three or more of the nine seats filed independently — twenty-five in all, grouped by what they are about rather than by who found them. Each carries the seats that filed it, its severity, the verbatim observation, where it lives in the code, and its canon status: open means no ruling governs it, ruled-against means the behaviour is doctrine and only Direction B may move it, known-open means the ledger already knows and has not answered. Each also carries a credit line — what stays true in the same corner of the product, consolidated from the nine seats' own lists, which both directions are forbidden to break.

      Width tiers — what the window takes away

      4 of 25 · 1 blocker

      Below 1440 the spine does not narrow. It empties. The three shelved blocks — the running index, the rooms block, the shelves — are gated in one line, and an open shelf is force-closed on the way down. This is ruled ground: I136 put those blocks at ≥1440 on purpose. It is still where four of the nine seats, and every practitioner, said they would give up.

      F01 Blocker 7 seats · U1 U3 U5 P1 P2 P3 P4 · conf .95 Ruled-against C8 (I136)

      Shelves, rooms block and running index are absent below 1440

      At 1280 the left rail is a 56px strip of unlabelled marks plus In hand / <1m: no IN THIS DOCUMENT, no Rooms, no THE SHELVES. Plan room, Spec book, Mood boards and Call sheet are not narrowed but removed, and an open shelf is force-closed on crossing below 1440.

      What stays true: the shelved spine's mechanics are right where they exist. Scroll-spy showed exactly one active entry at all eleven sample positions — no dead zones, no double highlights — and clicking a folded region's index row both unfolds it and scrolls to it in one act. Only the labels and the mount condition are wrong.

      components/document/doc-spine.tsx:135 · app/(document)/doc/[id]/page.tsx:553-562

      F02 High 7 seats · U1 U2 U3 U4 U5 P1 P2 · conf .95 Ruled-against C8

      At 1280 the spine is an unlabelled 56px icon rail

      At 1180–1439 the seven section marks render as bare coloured bars with no printed text; the active section's label is hidden min-[1440px]:block, and StrataMark's label becomes an aria-label only. ← Put down loses its word and becomes a bare ←. The word Project appears nowhere in the rail.

      What stays true: ← Put down is a trade verb doing real work and should never become “Close” or “Exit”; the Esc chain behind it is a correct, live-verified LIFO — ⌘K, then shelf, then put-down — with zero stranding at every layer tested.

      components/document/doc-spine.tsx:122-130,63 · components/document/strata-mark.tsx:81-82

      F15 High 3 seats · P1 P2 P3 · conf .95 Ruled-against C8 / D3

      The mobile spine sheet lists sections and nothing else

      The mobile spine sheet lists sections, Rooms when the project has any, and the margin — but never the running index or any shelf.

      What stays true: the sheet itself is a good compression — it folds the running index and margin capture into one reachable bottom sheet that answers “where am I / what's waiting” in a single tap, and every control in it clears the 44×44 minimum the codebase applies without exception.

      components/document/mobile/mobile-sheets.tsx:453-570

      F25 Medium 3 seats · U2 U5 P2 · conf .50 Ruled-against C8

      A held room has no visible release control once scrolled away

      The letterhead's In hand · {Room} line is plain text with no × or close affordance; the only release is clicking the same Rooms-block row again.

      What stays true: the lens lifts and never filters — nothing hides, and a held room keeps its own state word with In hand added rather than swapped in. That prefix is real text, so it reads correctly to a screen reader.

      Confidence is .50 and stated so: the local seed holds no project with both rooms and an active project section, so this is source-confirmed only, never driven. components/document/doc-letterhead.tsx:63-68 · lib/document/room-lens-context.tsx

      Install and care — the document forgets where she is standing

      3 of 25 · 2 blockers

      This is the review's sharpest finding and the one nobody had ruled on, because it is not a width rule at all. The shelved blocks are gated on active_section === 'project'. Advance the same document into install and every map on it disappears — at 1440 as much as at 390 — on precisely the two spreads where a designer is standing in a house holding a phone.

      F14 Blocker 3 seats · U1 U3 P1 · conf .97 — the highest in the set Open — no ruling governs it

      Index, rooms and shelves vanish on install and care documents

      On w1440-doc-install and w1440-doc-care the spine reads ← PUT DOWN, seven marks, the active label and ● IN HAND / under a min — no IN THIS DOCUMENT, no Rooms, no THE SHELVES. DocSpineShelvedBlocks mounts only when engagement_kind === 'project' && active_section === 'project'.

      What stays true: fold state persists correctly per document and per region across a reload, and a folded region reads visually distinct from an open-but-empty one — the returning designer's reading position is honoured. The problem is not that the product forgets her; it is that it forgets the job.

      app/(document)/doc/[id]/page.tsx:938-952

      F48 Blocker 1 seat · U1 · conf .92 Open

      The spec book has no door on install or care

      The Spec book → link renders inside {mode === 'project' && …}; in mode === 'install' the head prints only Install plus meta. There is no spec-book entry in STUDIO_ROOMS, the ledgers or the verbs, so matchSurfaces cannot find it and ⌘K has no spec-book row in either branch.

      What stays true: where the spec book is reachable, it is the right place — the junior seat called the workbench route legible on sight, and the procurement seat said it reads like the spreadsheet she trusts more than any app.

      One seat filed it; the code refuter confirmed it and the feasibility judge read the line in the tree. components/document/ffe-section.tsx:1030-1065 · lib/document/registry.tsx:77-327

      F03 High 7 seats · U1 U2 U3 U4 P1 P3 P4 · conf .95 Open

      The care-stage FF&E spread is headed Install

      On Birch Hollow (Care · ONGOING, The book closed Aug 25.) the FF&E spread's heading is the literal word Install and its empty state reads No FF&E lines are scheduled for installation. — four lines below a paragraph that correctly reads Plan the care work.

      What stays true: honest, plain-sentence empty states everywhere — NOTHING FILED, No boards yet, 0 of 5 essentials captured — keep going. Nothing pretends, which is why the numbers that are there are trusted. This heading is the one place the paper says something untrue, and R7 already rules that stamps only say true things.

      components/document/ffe-section.tsx:1037,1232 · app/(document)/doc/[id]/page.tsx:1436-1448

      The phase-wide question — the one nobody has ruled

      1 of 25 · 1 blocker · the worst task in the review
      F04 Blocker 6 seats · U1 U2 P1 P2 P3 P4 · conf .95 Known-open — T2 / T4, unruled since 2026·08·13

      Nothing answers a phase-wide question; ⌘K typed install returns No match

      ⌘K typed install returns only No match — Browse the Help Center / SEARCH THE GUIDES → and Ask the Engine · "INSTALL" · ASK & PLACE, while the Desk behind it prints the folder tab ASPEN · INSTALL. No Desk filter, tab or chip groups by phase.

      What stays true: the Desk's folio cards already narrate the day in plain sentences with dates and objects in them — 1 decision overdue — oldest due Aug 22, AP-012 has an open damage claim — each with exactly one act. Three seats called this the single best piece of writing in the product. It answers “what needs me today” completely; it just cannot be asked a question.

      Root cause, from the code refuter: a document row's ⌘K match string is folderTab + title only — the section word never enters it — and no registry alias contains install. components/document/command-bar.tsx:589-617 · lib/document/registry.tsx:344-351 · app/(document)/desk/page.tsx:339-370

      Money — four doors to bill, none to read what is owed

      4 of 25

      Every practitioner seat asked the same two-part question — bill the deposit, and who still owes me? — and every one of them answered the first half quickly and the second half by leaving the document. The region that holds the money is not called money.

      F09 High 4 seats · U4 P1 P2 P3 · conf .90 Open

      The money region is named Design authority and carries no money scent

      The folded seam reads Design authority   NO AUTHORITY YET · $0 COMMITTED   UNFOLD ↓; unfolded, the head is MONEY · ONE REGION / Design authority. The word money appears only in that small eyebrow, and the running-index row prints Design authority alone.

      What stays true: the ladder's honesty. no design authority recorded yet, no working budget yet, nothing executed yet — the region refuses to pretend it knows a number it does not have, which is exactly why the numbers it does print are believed.

      lib/document/document-index.ts:34-55 · components/document/commercial/money-region.tsx:295-305

      F16 High 3 seats · U1 P1 P2 · conf .90 Known-open — I141, money does not seam on install or care

      Who still owes me is unanswerable inside the document

      No row of the money ladder names a receivable; the answer sits in a nested band inside the same region rather than in the four-rung ladder that heads it.

      What stays true: ledger sheets slide over whatever she was looking at rather than replacing it — her document is still hers when she closes Orders, Accounts or Hours. The trip out is safe; it is just a trip.

      components/document/commercial/money-region.tsx:308-336

      F08 Medium 5 seats · U2 U5 P1 P3 P4 · conf .85 Ruled-against C7 (I135, one leader per region)

      Three-to-four competing doors answer one money question

      The Design authority head prints DRAW AN INVOICE, AMENDMENT and HOURS · THIS PROJECT ↗ side by side; the FF&E head adds BILL 3 UNINVOICED, ⌘K adds Draw an invoice for {Project}, and the Desk's BEGIN column a fourth. Nothing signposts which is the door.

      What stays true: scored ink. Every one of those acts is a bare DM Mono word with a proofreader's rule under it — no boxes, no plates. The junior seat's note: once she learned that underline means clickable, she stopped hunting for buttons anywhere on the surface.

      components/document/commercial/money-region.tsx:245-273 · components/document/ffe-section.tsx:994-1008 · lib/document/registry.tsx:301-313

      F26 Medium 3 seats · U3 U4 P2 · conf .90 Open

      The money explainer is a dense paragraph that names its own old UI

      Beneath four terse label rows sits one unbroken paragraph: Authority → plan → committed → moved. Moved is the accounts' committed figure … not funds disbursed… ending Absorbs today's four separate bands: design authority, working budget, authorizations & trade scopes, the accounts.

      What stays true: zero-shadow depth genuinely works at ≥1440 — value contrast, rule weight and flat stacked edges carry the region separation cleanly with no shadow anywhere in the primary reading flow. The density break here is a copy problem, not a hierarchy one.

      components/document/commercial/money-region.tsx:327-336

      Lexicon — one word for three things, three words for one

      5 of 25

      The drawer's The Rooms (g r) opens THE ROOMS · 6 scanned rooms, cards titled by person (Lily Tanaka / Kitchen · scanned Aug 24); the spine's Rooms block lists FF&E groups; Plan room is a shelf of drawings. P4 took The Rooms first looking for a sofa, and backed out.

      What stays true: Call sheet · who is on the job is the model pairing for the whole surface — a studio word outside, a trade word in the sub-line. Every seat that named a lexicon fix reached for that pattern rather than inventing one.

      The row reads Knowledge   STUDIO LIBRARY →; the leaf's eyebrow reads STUDIO LIBRARY · CROSS-PROJECT, its body STUDIO LIBRARY — CROSS-PROJECT STANDARDS. NOTHING FILED FOR THIS PROJECT., its act OPEN THE STUDIO LIBRARY →. It holds nothing and duplicates a permanent drawer door.

      The two Desk begin verbs carry no distinguishing sub-label

      The header prints ＋ CAPTURE A LEAD and ＋ OPEN A PROJECT bare. Their distinguishing sub-labels — BEGIN A BRIEF and NO PROPOSAL NEEDED — exist only inside ⌘K's BEGIN group, and Capture a lead is deliberately omitted from the Desk's own BEGIN column.

Capture a lead · begin a Brief against Open a project · no proposal needed does the disambiguating work before the click — the pattern the shelf rows, the ledger rows and Desk Contents all need and mostly lack.       Reach — keyboard, phone, and the two focus returns

      4 of 25 · 1 blocker
      F49 Blocker 1 seat · U2 · conf .85 Ruled-against C8 (scoped to 390)

      No visible way to open ⌘K anywhere on a phone

      Inside a document at 390 there is no visible way to open ⌘K — the mobile bar, its More menu and the sheets call no opener. The Desk header's Find anything button is the only phone entry point, and it exists only on /desk.

      What stays true: the register itself mounts unconditionally in the document layout with no width gate — the recall path works at every width; only the printed door is missing. At 390 the More menu does reach the ledgers, in two taps.

      components/document/mobile/mobile-bar.tsx · components/document/mobile/mobile-sheets.tsx

      F10 High 4 seats · U1 U5 P1 P3 · conf .90 Open

      The seven g chords work, and are printed nowhere on screen

      g l, g p, g r, g o, g a, g h, g t all route correctly — probe-verified live. A full-text sweep of /desk and /doc/[id] finds no chord hint; the badges print only inside ⌘K rows, which she must open with ⌘K to see. / and ? register no handler at all.

      What stays true: they work. All seven chords and ⌘K fired correctly under the probe once its own focus bug was corrected — the mechanism is sound and the registry is its single source. The gap is one of publication, not of engineering.

      components/document/registry-shortcuts.tsx:42-47,85-221 · components/document/command-bar.tsx:766-768 · probe/01-interactive-probe.md §3

      F21 Medium 3 seats · U2 U5 P2 · conf .95 Open

      ⌘K never restores focus to its trigger on close

      command-bar.tsx has one focus line — focusing the input on open — and no capture or restore of the pre-open document.activeElement. Live-verified: focus the Plan room shelf button, press ⌘K, press Escape, and focus lands on <body>.

      What stays true: everything else restores.       Four voices

      Where they stopped, in their own words

      The four practitioner seats wrote in the first person, present tense, and were asked for one thing above all: the moment they stop and what they are asking themselves. “I expected a ___ and there wasn't one” was the deliverable. Six of those moments, verbatim.

      P1 — solo residential principal, Madison, six live jobs, one always in install · T4, change the fabric on the living room sofa

      on the install document, immediately: browser tab → old portal.

      She had already hesitated three times before that — “Unsorted is not a room; my whole mental model is room → line” — and the inked leader on the head asked her to add a fourth line to a job with three already in production. Then she opened the install spread, the week she actually retraces a credenza, and found her FF&E schedule gone. This is the give-up the whole review was commissioned to explain. F05, F14, F34

      P2 — principal of a three-person studio, Milwaukee, eleven live jobs · T2, show me everything in install

      here. There is no surface — Desk, tier, or lens — that answers “everyone in install.”

      Her next sentence names the cost precisely: “I would open each of my eleven documents' spines and read the phase mark myself, or ask a junior — which is the exact thing my tolerance forbids.” She scored what-to-do 2 and how-to-get-there 1, because she knew to try ⌘K and there was nowhere to get to. F04, blocker, six seats

      P3 — junior designer, week one, Minneapolis, no legacy portal to flee to · T2

      I'd ask my manager, “which jobs are in install right now?” There's no dead-end message telling me to do that — I'd just eventually stop trying.

      Her only escape route is a person. She also read the fallback and flinched: “‘ask the Engine’ sounds like I'd be handing off to an AI, and I don't know what it would even do with the word ‘install’.” That phrase is the first text anyone reads inside search, and it breaks the brand's own hard rule against engine framing. Both directions delete it. F04, F33

      P4 — FF&E- and procurement-heavy designer, Oak Park, six-figure budgets and quarterly installs · T4

      I'd back out confused — this is a real wrong turn, not a hypothetical one.

      She went looking for a sofa, saw the only word Rooms visible in the chrome, clicked it, and landed in a gallery of scanned geometry titled by household. Three surfaces own that noun and none of them says which one it means. F17

      P1 again · T9, bill the deposit — and who still owes me?

      I hesitate before clicking anything, because Design authority does not sound like money. It sounds like sign-off authority — who gets to approve the design.

      The junior arrived at the same misreading from the other end — “my first read of it was ‘who's allowed to make design decisions’.” Both then found four doors to draw an invoice and none to read what is owed. Both directions rename the region Money; both add a rung that names the receivable. F09, F08, F16

      P4 again · T9, on trusting a number

      I'd stop trusting the in-document money figures for reconciliation and go straight to the Accounts book instead.

      Because the word Committed means nothing executed yet in one region and $14,420 COMMITTED in a folded seam three screens below it, on the same document, on the same afternoon. For a designer who refuses any composition that separates a piece from its PO state, a collision on the money word itself is the same defect one level up.       Twenty planks

      Before either direction was drafted, one pass took the surviving findings and pulled out the fixes so obviously correct that arguing about them would be theatre — a wrong word, a duplicated string, a missing registry row, a dead shelf. Never structure: no new surface, no new tier, no moved region. If a fix needed doctrine, it was not a plank.

      Twenty planks close twenty findings. Ten of the twenty are a single string. Two — SP-16's registry row and SP-19's in-flow link — are the only ones that add anything at all, and both add a second door to a destination that already exists.

      Direction A

      Everything Prints

      Nearly every door this review found missing is already built and already routed — the plan room, the spec book, the call sheet, the claim drawer on an FF&E line, the send-wall line. What is missing is the printing.

      Thesis

      A keeps the shelved-spine organ exactly as I136 built it — index, rooms, shelves, all at ≥1440 — and pays for the narrower tiers the way doctrine already says a demoted act must be paid for: each door moves onto the body it acts on, and the one width-independent register the product owns (⌘K) becomes a printed doorway instead of a chord.

      Every artifact and every next act on this surface already exists in code, so printing each one where she is already looking moves each of the five worst tasks across a named threshold at 1280 — without adding a surface, a tier, a mode, or one doctrine amendment.

      Stated ordinally, because no re-walk has been run: T6 and T14 cross from needs a guess to the door is on screen; T5 and T13 from gave up, left the document to a second guess that lands; T2 from could not find it to one printed door answers it, one stage at a time — explicitly not to a fleet read. If any of the five still needs a chord she was never shown or a word she never saw printed, the direction has failed. These are the direction's own claims, not measured outcomes.

      Amendments to ruled canon: zero. New ledger entries proposed: six, all additive, every one a revert.

      Keeps · Refuses · Costs

      Keeps
      The Esc chain's LIFO · ← Put down · the send-wall state line as the model for state-plus-one-act · Add a room at the foot of the room list · nothing hover-gated · the index's scroll-spy · fold persistence · a piece, its PO state and its price on one row · honest empties.
      Refuses
      No fleet or roster tier — P2's Monday read is Direction B's to answer. No shelved block below 1440 or on the mobile spine sheet. No room filter. No split, peek or tab. No drawer badge. No toast. No boxed act. No second inked leader. No boards on the paper outside speccing. No reorder of the paper's mount order. No sealing semantics, no active_section write, no dependency on I114.
      Costs
      Mostly strings, four small derivations, one deleted condition, one edited predicate. The FF&E leader election is a real new derivation plus reused targeting, not reordering. ⌘K's stage group is a reducer over documents already loaded. The Drafting Room's Desk row needs a shared opener ported out of ⌘K's fallback. The contrast pass (F56, ~374 sites) and the skip link (F55) are named and costed separately, not folded into the estimate.
      Ledger
      Zero doctrine amendments — but six new I-entries are proposed (mount conditions, leader election, the lexicon pass, ⌘K's stage answers, the mobile In this document group, the drawer's Find anything door), plus one entry recording the Thumb Index's removal, which has no trace in the ledger at all. Six writes and one ratification of Kody's time.

      First slice — the sentence and the spine

      1. The seven stage sentences and acts, the reordered tie-break, the Review now retirement, the zero-row fall-through. F18, F41, F77
      2. The shelved blocks mount on install and care; the index derives from those spreads' own mount order; the inner mode === 'project' guard on the spec-book link goes; the care head keys off sectionKey. F14, F48, SP-01
      3. Six string-only planks — SP-06, SP-07, SP-08, SP-09, SP-12, SP-18 — all in the same files.

      Six files. 5–7 days (the feasibility judge reads it as 7–9 with the Worktable test rebase and guide unit tests). The metric it moves: time-to-true-read first — the top sentence becomes an act instead of a shrug on five of seven stages, and install and care stop opening blank. Unaided acts second: on an install document the index, rooms and shelves reappear, so the spec book, plan room, roster and boards stop being recall.

      Landing on both baselines

      Flag off — today's paper

      Every move lands here first. The guide, the zone, the spine, the paper's mount order, the registry, ⌘K, the drawer, the mobile bar and every region head sit outside the worktable gate, so flag-off is the full direction.

      Flag on — the Worktable

      Everything is inherited unchanged, because TableFrame wraps the same regions rather than replacing them. Delivery: the leader election yields to the release lift when it shows and elects the sharpest exception when it does not. Finalize: the shelves swap to The client's copy, so Knowledge's retirement touches the project list alone. Speccing: the on-paper boards strip stays as ruled, and every board door now reads Boards — three names become one. Both papers then say the same seven sentences and open the same doors, which is the precondition for the flag-on walk that is still owed.

      Coverage

      Blockers and highs addressed: F02–F09, F14, F16–F18, F28–F30, F33, F35, F48–F52, F55, F57, F59, F61 — F04 partially, by design. Routed around: F01 — no tier is added; the doors move to the bodies they act on, plus the register. Out of scope by doctrine: F15, F32, F54, F60. Deferred, with reasons named: F10 (chord hints need chrome A does not touch), F53 (a new act surface), F56 (its own accessibility pass, costed separately), F58 (a data ruling). Not addressed: F11, F21, F25, F45, F66, F70, F71, F79–F80, F84–F86, F94–F95, F97–F99, F101.

      Two costs A states against itself

      Ungating the spec book routes the procurement designer there from more places — while F58 stands unresolved, so the same walnut sectional still reads RECEIVED on the paper and DELIVERED in the spec book. She meets that trust-breaking moment more often than today. And the practitioner judge caught A building one move on ground that does not exist: an acknowledgement chip for the Orders sheet, argued from a finding the code refuter killed — every PO row already prints its send and ack lifecycle. That move should be cut; re-pointing the unanswered-PO need at the line itself is the part that stands.

      Direction B

      The Shop Ticket

      In a workshop the ticket travels with the job: one card clipped to the work, saying what is on this job and where each part of it sits — and it reads the same at the bench, in the finishing room and on the truck. Patina's document has no such card. Its map is made of chrome.

      Thesis

      Orientation belongs to the job, not to the screen. If the eight things a designer reaches for — rooms · pieces · drawings · spec · boards · money · dates · people — are printed on the paper itself rather than in width-gated chrome, then every item-reach cell is one act at 1440, 1280 and 390 and on all seven sections; and the same eight rows, stacked across jobs, answer the phase-wide question without a new tier.

      Falsified by: any of the eight classes costing more than one act from an open document at any tier; install and care still losing reach the project spread has; or a designer asked “what's in install” still having to type, filter or remember. These are the direction's own claims.

      Structurally, not by degree. Direction A moves existing doors to the bodies they already act on and adds no organ. B deletes two spine organs, adds one that has never existed, and moves two width rules held since I136. B removes furniture A leaves standing.

      The map

      The Desk — the studio's one cross-job surface

      One roster of every live job, grouped by stage, replaces the folio grid, STUDIO PULSE and RECENT BOARDS. Needs are a red-letter mark on the job's own line, not a separate list; nothing folds on first paint. T2 is answered at zero acts, by a heading rather than a filter — B's own claim, not a measured outcome; no re-walk has been run. F04, F23, F39, F62, F65

      Density rule, for the eleven-job studio: one line per job, wrapping to two or three, never a card; headings never fold; within a group, red-letter first, then oldest. Eleven jobs is eleven lines under five or six headings — one screen at 1440, one scroll at 1280.

      The seven sentences — and seven rest states

      B keeps deriveDocumentGuide's precedence for rungs one to five and replaces rung six — the static stageCopy table whose labels are five shrugs. In its place, deriveTicketLeader computes the sentence and the act from the same eight rows on screen, so the guide can never name what the map does not show. And the red-letter zone registers the mobile primary, which today only the letterhead instruments do — the reason the 390 bar shows a truncated MESSAGE THE CLI… over an urgent zone with no act.

      Fourteen states rather than seven, so no stage shrugs even when nothing is wrong. The word Review appears nowhere. The tie-break: money at risk today → a dated promise to the client → a piece that cannot move → work that can wait, in ticket order. Ties inside a rank go to the older date. One internal contradiction the feasibility judge caught: the project headline elects the unanswered PO (rank three) while the tie-break puts the specimen's two dated approvals at rank two.

That one asymmetry is why the mapping is hard.

      Five screens, drawn

      The same specimen, the same figures, the same twenty planks — a different shape. Where the specimen gives no number, the product's own honest empty prints instead (Nothing filed, No boards yet, Nobody on it yet), never an invented one.

      The amendment ledger — two, both clauses of one entry

      Lane B may amend doctrine, and the rule is binding: name the entry by id, quote the clause, state the trade in one sentence, state the rollback. Unnamed or unpriced is rejected on sight. Both amendments below are clauses of I136, and both are counted.

      B1 — the mount gate

      “The spine grows three blocks — ≥1440px only.” DECISIONS.md:8427ff · C8

      Gains
      Rooms, drawings, spec book, boards and roster stop being a ≥1440-and-project-section privilege — one act at every tier on all seven sections. Closes F01, F14, F48, F72 and half of F82; moves T6, T13 and T14.
      Gives up
      The shelved spine as an organ — both blocks deleted, and about 180px of every document's measure goes to the ticket. I136's principle — the paper holds the work, the shelves hold the artifacts — survives in meaning, not in furniture: artifacts are listed on the paper and still open beside it at ≥1440.
      Rollback
      The job-ticket flag off restores the gate and both blocks byte-identically.

      B2 — the lens's width release

      “The hold releases if the window drops below 1440px, where nothing on screen could put it down.” DECISIONS.md:8461-8462

      Gains
      F60 — a held room lifts at 1280 and 390. The clause's own stated reason stops being true the moment the ticket's room chip exists.
      Gives up
      The guarantee that a lift is only ever seen beside a full spine. A designer resizing mid-hold keeps the hold rather than losing it, so the letterhead must name the room in hand at every width — which I136 already requires.
      Rollback
      The flag off restores the auto-release. I136's never-filters clause is untouched.

      One ruling request, not an amendment — C14

      Q3 / I138 says “the flag off is main's composition exactly” (DECISIONS.md:8740-8742). Read narrowly, that binds the worktable guard: flag-off must be byte-identical to main's Worktable-free composition. Read broadly, it freezes any feature shipping ahead of the flag-on walk Kody still owes. The ticket ships behind its own fail-closed flag and does not change worktable's off-state composition, so B asserts the narrow reading and asks Kody to confirm it. Read broadly, the ticket waits for the walk and the design is unchanged. The feasibility judge accepts the framing as honestly named, and notes it resolves into a third amendment if the broad reading wins.

      Stated so no verifier has to guess: B's flag-on landing deletes nothing ratified. The Speccing rooms rail (I139) and the Delivery money seam (I141) both stand, with the ticket's rows anchoring to them; the Intake spread's inert opens when… seams are left to the Worktable's own wave.

      Keeps · Refuses · Costs

      Keeps
      The Esc/put-down LIFO · ← Put down · the send-wall line, in whose image the ticket's rows are drawn · Add a room in flow · the index's derivation and scroll-spy · fold persistence · one piece and its PO state on one line · zero shadows, scored ink, one leader per region, the Record at the foot · honest empties · the no-badge law · 44×44 · the lens that lifts and never filters.
      Refuses
      A fleet or roster tier — the phase-wide question is answered by grouping the Desk's own jobs. A Desk-side artifact browser — reaching a board still costs opening its job, because D1 is right. Split views, peeks, tabs. The shelves restored at 1280 as shelves. Badges. A second editable home for spec attributes. Any I114 dependency. The send–seal wall.
      Costs
      A new component and derivation; two shipped components deleted; the shelves' width gate removed and the leaf given a route mode below 1440 it has never had; the force-close removed; the lens's matchMedia release unwound; guide rung six replaced; the Worktable test suite rebased. No migration, no data-model change. One new fail-closed flag.
      Declared gaps
      P2's Monday question is half-answered — the roster answers “who's in install” at zero acts and prints each job's own receivable, but nothing prints a studio-wide total or a “since Friday” delta. P4 pays a glance — the Pieces row is a layer above the region, not a replacement, so her install-minus-ten reconciliation still runs line by line below. The trade: her exceptions are visible before the first scroll, on install and care spreads where no summary exists at all today.

      First slice

      Ship the ticket on project-kind documents — project, install and care — all eight rows, all three widths, behind job-ticket. Nothing else. Not the Desk roster, the guide rewrite or the renames. Install and care come free with project: the change removes one mount condition, not three implementations, which is why F14 closes on day one rather than in wave three. The proposal-chain spreads are wave two, so T5's mood board is not moved by this slice.

      Why it changes a Tuesday: on 25 August, Leah opens the Vandersteen to learn whether the console claim can still be filed and whether Sturdy Oak answered. Today “where is anything” is a 200px spine she only has at 1440, and on the install document not at all. After this slice one band says 1 damaged, $17,500 owed you, 22 days and $12,300 deposit not drawn before she scrolls, and each of the eight is one click — on the laptop in the car as much as the studio monitor.

      Landing on both baselines

      Flag off — today's paper

      The ticket mounts between the letterhead and the guide. The spine keeps put-down, the marks, On this paper, the timer and the presence line, and loses the two blocks. At ≥1440 a row still opens a 320px leaf beside the spine — and the reading position no longer re-wraps under it, because the ticket rather than a region head is what the leaf sits beside. Below 1440 the row routes to the leaf's own page and returns with the full project name. Regions, mount order, leaders and the Record are untouched.

      Flag on — the Worktable

      The ticket mounts above the table frame: the job's header over the job's middle, I138's own division. Intake: the ticket's empty rows say what the inert opens when… seams say. Speccing: the Rooms row anchors to I139's rooms rail rather than replacing it, and the Boards row anchors to the on-paper strip — so the door that dies is the Desk strip, not a ruled one. Finalize: The client's copy becomes a ninth row on proposal documents. Delivery: the release lift keeps the table head, the money seam stands, and the Money row is the seam's index carrying the receivable the seam is scoped not to. The install setting finally moves an item-reach cell — which is exactly what F32 says the Worktable does not do today.

      The two, compared

      Seven axes, two judges, never averaged

J2 reads for product and engineering and cites a file or a ruling behind every cost; axes 4, 5, 6 and 7 carry its weight.       Distinct by construction

      Both judges checked this independently and both answered yes, provably rather than rhetorically. A edits the mount predicate and leaves the width gate standing. B deletes the two components that predicate feeds. Opposite operations on the same lines. A's reach lives on the bodies that own each act; B's lives in one new band that owns none of them. A carries zero amendments and one wave of copy; B carries two amendments and a new derivation. The mocks could not be mistaken for each other at any width. The only overlap is the twenty shared planks, which the instrument requires.

      Who is worse off

      Under A

      P2, the three-person-studio principal. Her Monday read across eleven jobs is refused by lane. She gets one stage at a time through ⌘K's stage group, and no studio-wide receivable figure exists anywhere in A — so she still opens eleven documents while the register tells her who is in install and never what it costs.

      Under B

      P1 and P4, at their own tiers. The spine is sticky; the paper is not, and the Vandersteen project spread runs past 2,400px. Today's shelves and rooms block ride with her as she scrolls into the FF&E; B's ticket scrolls off the top. For P4 reconciling line by line at install-minus-ten, reach from where she is standing becomes scroll-back-plus-one. It also undercuts B2's own justification, since the room chip B nominates as the put-down affordance is off-screen exactly when a held room needs one. And for P1's first three seconds, an eight-row index is interposed between the letterhead and the red-letter zone — the one organ every walk says already works.

      Recommendation

      A's slice now. B's ticket next, after two things.

      Both judges favour Direction A, and neither recommends dropping Direction B. They arrive at the same sequencing from opposite lenses, which is the strongest signal in the pack.

      The practitioner judge: A's first slice moves the two things the walks complain about loudest — the shrug at the top of the paper and the blank rail on install week — inside a week, while B's twelve days buy reach and leave the shrug standing. The feasibility judge: A is the only one of the two that can be on a designer's screen this month, and its first slice closes two blockers with one deleted condition and one edited predicate, both read in the tree. And then, plainly: B is the better product answer at 1280 and 390 — one act on all seven sections is reach A cannot buy — but it is a quarter, not a Tuesday.

      The sequence

      1. Land the twenty planks and A's first slice, now. Un-flagged, 5–7 days by A's estimate and 7–9 with tests. It needs no ruling from anyone. The seven sentences, the tie-break, the zero-row fall-through, the shelved blocks mounting on install and care, the spec-book gate deleted, the care head keyed off its own section.
      2. A's remaining waves next — the lexicon pass, ⌘K's stage group and This surface rows, the mobile In this document group, the drawer's printed Find anything door, the compact spine's printed label.
      3. Then B's ticket — but not straight to build. Two things Kody owes come first: the flag-on Worktable walk that has been owed since I143, and a C14 ruling on the narrow reading. And one thing the reviewers owe: redraw the ticket as a sticky seam — collapsed to B's own two-line 390 form once the letterhead scrolls past, at every width — and put it in front of a junior and a solo principal at 1280 before B1 and B2 go to Kody at all. The sticky-spine regression is the one thing that could make B's own strongest tier worse than today, and it is cheap to settle.

      Build B on top of A's mount fix, not instead of it — A's fix is what proves the four project-scoped hooks behave on install and care spreads before B stakes an organ on them. And do not run them concurrently: both directions edit the same five files.

      The one sequencing conflict, stated openly: A's F14 fix is one predicate on components B deletes. One line thrown away for weeks of install-week value is the right trade — and A's lexicon, its seven sentences and all twenty planks survive into B unchanged.

      The grafts, both ways

      From B into A — all of it Lane-A-legal

      1. Pieces for Project · FF&E, head and index row together, sub-line the FF&E schedule, by room. It closes the junior's own worst label and costs A nothing doctrinally — a string in the index plus the head. Both judges named this first, independently.
      2. B's rest states — a named sentence and act for each section when nothing is wrong. A's seven defaults cover the quiet case for project only, and that is what stops its default reading as a shrug.
      3. The red-letter zone registering the mobile primary. A prints the elected act untruncated at 390; B fixes F07 at its root.
      4. B's 390 wrap discipline — line one is identity and never elides, line two is the two worst exceptions in tie-break order, a third is dropped whole, nothing cuts mid-word. Apply it to A's mobile bar and FF&E head.
      5. B's I114 stance — sections name parts of the paper, the Six name phases of the work, and they never print in one glance — in place of A's explanatory sentence under the schedule. A label that needs a footnote is a label a first-week designer cannot read.
      6. B's flag-absent People string — “the call sheet isn't turned on for this studio” — so absence and emptiness never look alike.
      7. B's honesty about the missing boards route. A should declare its 1280 and 390 boards cell as needing a below-1440 destination that does not exist, rather than costing it as a registry row.

      From A into B — for whoever builds the ticket

      1. ⌘K's WHERE THE WORK STANDS empty-query group. It answers T2 for the solo principal without waiting for the Desk rebuild in wave two — which is B's own weakest moment on effort-to-first-value.
      2. A's ladder prints six rungs where B prints five — Owed and Not drawn both on screen. Moved cannot be re-derived from the specimen; see the data question in §11.

      And two corrections to carry into either build

      1. Cut A's Orders acknowledgement chip. It answers a critique with a finding the code refuter killed. Re-pointing the unanswered-PO need at the line itself is the part that stands.
      2. Cut B's two citations of killed rows — the empty install spread and the absent call sheet. The ticket's case does not need either.

      What this recommendation costs

      In time
      One week for the planks and A's slice; a second wave of A over the following weeks; B's twelve days — sixteen to twenty by the feasibility judge's count — not started until the owed walk and the C14 ruling land. Nothing runs concurrently.
      In doctrine
      Nothing now. Six new ledger entries recording what A did, plus one entry recording a verbal ruling that has never been written down. Later, if B proceeds: two named amendments to I136 and one ruling on how C14 reads.
      In refusals
      P2 waits. The phase-wide question — the review's worst task, at 1.50 — is answered one stage at a time by A's register and not at all across the fleet until B's Desk roster in wave two. No studio-wide receivable exists in either first slice. This is the honest shape of the trade, and it should be said to her rather than around her.
      In scope that stays open
      F56's contrast pass across roughly 374 sites and F55's missing skip link belong to neither direction and have no owner. F58's RECEIVED/DELIVERED disagreement needs a data ruling, not a rename — and A's ungating of the spec book makes a designer meet it more often. Below 1440 there is still no boards destination in the app at all.

      Questions for the team

      Ten things we need answered before anyone builds

      Three of these are amendments or readings of ruled canon, and only Kody can settle them. Three are ledger hygiene — a ruling that was made and never written down, a mapping session that is owed, and a persona whose question this review deliberately refuses. Three are defects the evidence surfaced that belong to no direction and currently have no owner, and one is a data question the specimen itself raises.

      01 · Amendment · needs a ruling

      B1 — may the shelved spine's mount gate move?

      I136 reads “The spine grows three blocks — ≥1440px only.” Direction B asks to move it: the map leaves the spine and clips to the paper, so rooms, drawings, spec book, boards and roster become one act at every tier on all seven sections. It buys F01, F14, F48, F72 and half of F82, and moves three of the five worst tasks. It costs the shelved spine as an organ — two shipped components deleted, about 180px of measure — and rolls back with the flag.

      We ask: yes, no, or yes-after-the-sticky-seam-redraw.

      02 · Amendment · needs a ruling

      B2 — may a held room survive below 1440?

      I136 reads “The hold releases if the window drops below 1440px, where nothing on screen could put it down.” The clause names its own reason, and the ticket's room chip removes it. B asks to unwind the auto-release so a lift works at 1280 and 390 — closing F60, and giving the 1280 laptop the one capability it has no substitute for. The risk is exactly what the clause was written to prevent: a hold nobody can put down at a width where the affordance has scrolled away. That is the practitioner judge's reason for redrawing the ticket as a sticky seam first.

      We ask: does B2 stand or fall with B1, and does the sticky seam settle it?

      03 · Reading of canon · needs a ruling

      C14 — narrow or broad?

      Q3 / I138 reads “the flag off is main's composition exactly.” Read narrowly, that binds the worktable guard and nothing else. Read broadly, it freezes any feature shipping ahead of the flag-on Worktable walk that is still owed. B asserts the narrow reading — its ticket has its own fail-closed flag and does not touch worktable's off-state composition — and asks for confirmation. Under the broad reading, the ticket simply waits for the walk; the design is unchanged either way. Direction A also ships un-flagged onto GA, which the broad reading would touch too.

      We ask: which reading, and does it apply to A's unflagged slice as well?

      04 · Ledger hygiene

      The Thumb Index removal has never been written down

      Kody removed the Thumb Index verbally, with the instruction do not re-propose. A grep of the whole decision ledger for thumb index returns zero hits. It is out of canon by omission rather than by ruling, which means the next reviewer — human or otherwise — has nothing to read that would stop them proposing it again. Neither direction re-proposes it, and both were told not to.

      We ask for one ledger entry recording the removal and its reason.

      05 · Ledger hygiene · a candidate, not a dependency

      I114 — is this the section↔stage mapping?

      The mapping session has been owed since I114 and named as blocking in three separate waves; every wave so far has left active_section standing as the sealing authority rather than touch it. Direction B offers a candidate, explicitly as a candidate: brief → Consultation, discovery → Schematic Design, direction → Design Development, proposal → no phase (the agreement sits between Design Development and Procurement), project → Procurement & Orders, install → Installation & Styling, care → Completion. That single asymmetry is why the mapping is hard, and why nothing in either direction depends on it. Two seats filed the collision independently: seven section names and the Patina Six print on one paper today.

      We ask whether this candidate is worth putting on the agenda — not for a ruling now.

      06 · A refusal we want acknowledged

      T4 and T2 — what do we tell the three-person studio?

      “No fleet view” and “install is a label on project mode, not a mode” are the two most severe findings ever recorded against this surface, and neither has ever been ruled on. This review re-derived them independently, from six seats, as a blocker at 1.50 — the worst task score in the set. Direction A refuses a fleet tier by lane and answers the question one stage at a time through the register. Direction B answers it at zero acts by grouping the Desk's own jobs — but in wave two, not the first slice. Under either sequence, the principal of a three-person studio opens eleven documents on Monday morning for at least another quarter, and no surface anywhere prints a studio-wide receivable.

      We ask: is that acceptable for a quarter, and should T2/T4 finally get a ledger entry either way?

      07 · A defect, not a direction

      F03 — the care spread is headed Install, today, in production shape

      Seven of nine seats filed it. The care spread mounts the FF&E section with mode="install", so the heading literal reads Install and the empty state reads No FF&E lines are scheduled for installation. — four lines under a paragraph that correctly says Plan the care work. R7 already rules that the document's stamps only say true things. Both directions carry the same fix, as shared plank SP-01: key the ternary off sectionKey, which is already threaded in. Two strings and one condition.

      We ask whether this should be hotfixed now, ahead of and independent of either direction.

      08 · A defect the evidence surfaced · no owner

      The /room/<id> route throws a PostgREST error on screen

      Capturing the room-file route produced a verified screenshot of the page reading “This room is still being drawn.” with a live application error printed over it: Cannot coerce the result to a single JSON object. The shot ledger records it as a genuine defect rather than a harness artifact. It is outside this review's scope — Room View internals were explicitly excluded — and it is on screen.

      We ask for an owner and a bug, not a design decision.

      09 · A defect the evidence surfaced · no owner

      F56 — clay and terracotta fail contrast wherever they carry text

      Clay #C4A57B and terracotta #D4A090 are used as text in roughly 374 places at about 2.2:1. The red-letter band's own eyebrow uses a darker #C4836F at about 2.95:1 — still under the 4.5:1 that WCAG 2.2 AA requires. Neither direction touches it: a token change across 374 sites needs its own accessibility pass, and both say so rather than folding it into an estimate. Its sibling, F55, is smaller and equally unowned — a grep for a skip link across the whole document app returns zero hits, so a keyboard-only user traverses the entire spine on every load.

      We ask for a decision on whether the contrast pass is scheduled, deferred, or accepted as a known exception.

      10 · A data question · no owner

      Moved — which number is it?

      On this specimen the ladder's Moved rung equals Authorized: both read $141,600. An in motion figure means ordered money that has actually left the studio, and that needs vendor payouts — a number the accounts band holds and the Money region never reads. The only payment figures the specimen carries are the client's side of the ledger (Invoiced to date $96,400, Paid to date $78,900) — money coming in, not money paid out to makers — so subtracting it would invent arithmetic. Both directions now print the ordered figure under SP-04's gloss, ordered through installed (committed, not yet paid out), which is honest and leaves the rung reading twice.

      We ask: expose vendor payouts to the Money region so Moved carries its own number, or retire the rung.

      Colophon

      How this was made, and what it rests on

      Method, in order

      1. Boot and state ladder. Local Supabase confirmed, the environment gate checked against the production URL before anything ran, three transient rich seeds re-applied, and five documents lifted up the stage ladder by RPC — never by direct writes to business tables.
      2. Evidence. Two screenshot passes, one per flag state, at 1440, 1280 and 390. Every PNG was opened and classified by hand as verified, blank or wrong surface — the script's own success ledger was not trusted, because the harness writes a fallback image on failure. 65 verified flag-off, 21 verified flag-on, 86 in total. Two states were genuinely unreachable in this seed and are recorded as unreachable rather than counted.
      3. Probe. A live browser drove hover affordances, the Esc chain, the seven chords, scroll-spy at eleven sample positions, fold persistence across reload, focus return on four surfaces, the room lens on resize, console errors across eight routes, and cold/warm timings. Nine probes plus one supplementary. Two probe-side bugs were found, corrected in session, and recorded — the first chord run reported all seven dead because the probe's own click had moved focus off <body>, which the shortcut contract correctly treats as an overlay context.
      4. Grounding. The code anatomy was re-verified against HEAD rather than inherited, and the decision ledger — 9,431 lines — was read by grep and range, never whole. Several constraint citations inherited from the brief were corrected in that pass: two pointed at a heading rather than the rule, and one line number cited for I114 does not exist in the file.
      5. Panel. Nine seats, identical evidence pack, identical sixteen-task script, run in parallel and in isolation. 203 raw findings, deduplicated by a key of surface, width, flag and slug so identical observations collided across seats and their votes were counted. 101 canonical findings; every raw id preserved.
      6. Verification. Three refuters, each over the whole set, each in a fresh context: one against the code, one against the ledger, one re-driving the browser. A finding survived only if none killed it. 92 survived. A finding ruled against by canon still survives — it is simply not free for Direction A.
      7. Directions. Shared planks first, then two authors in separate contexts with opposing lane constraints, then four critics trying to break them, then both authors revising against their own critiques, then two judges scoring the same rubric without seeing each other. Every revision is logged in the direction documents with the critique id that forced it.
      8. Mocks. Ten screens hand-built in CSS from a kit derived from the portal's own tokens and type roles. Zero box-shadow declarations in the entire kit — depth is value contrast and 1px rules, as doctrine requires. Both lanes drew the same specimen and the same twenty planks.

      What this deck does not claim

      No task score here is a measurement of a person. No improvement claimed by a direction has been walked — each is labelled as that direction's own claim, and both directions state what would falsify them. Nothing was built into the product, no migration was written, and the decision ledger was not appended to: Kody rules first. The nine killed findings appear only as killed. Where a direction rests on ground a refuter removed, this deck says so on the direction's own page.
